description:
OBSOLETED on 2026-04-26: superseded by the single-repo migration plan
(_project/TODO/main/planning/single-repo-migration-phase-*.yaml). The
divergence preflight protects against external commits on the public
mirror being destroyed by force-push; the migration deletes the
force-push and the bidirectional sync model entirely. Phase 6 deletes
automate_release.py and benchbox-sync.

Original description below preserved for historical context.

---

`scripts/automate_release.py` calls `prepare_release.py` (line 1073), which
deletes and rebuilds the target public tree from scratch. Anything on public
main that is not present in private at that point is destroyed. Today,
nothing checks for that condition.

Failure mode: a community PR is merged into the public repo between releases.
The next `automate_release.py --push` run silently squashes those commits
away during the force-rewrite of public main. Author attribution and
external work are lost.

Goal: insert a preflight check that detects unexpected commits on public
main since the last `v*` tag (or unexpected file-level conflicts) BEFORE
the destructive rebuild, and abort with an actionable message unless the
user explicitly opts in via a new `--allow-public-divergence` flag.

Approach: extract a programmatic `check_public_repo_state(source, target)`
function from the existing `cmd_status` in `benchbox/release/sync.py`,
returning a `PublicRepoState` dataclass. `automate_release.py` imports and
calls it (no subprocess - existing precedent at automate_release.py:43-49
already imports from `benchbox.release.workflow`).

Plan file: /Users/joe/.claude/plans/make-a-detailed-and-dynamic-bentley.md
(Phase B).

anti_patterns.why: they are out of scope for this item; only `cmd_status` is being refactored to share logic with the new function.
they are different concerns (force-tag overwrites a local tag; divergence override accepts losing public commits); keep flags semantically distinct.
the entire point is to fail loudly when external commits would be destroyed; opt-in is the safe default.

anti_patterns.dont: make check_public_repo_state mutate the target repo
anti_patterns.why: it is a preflight; even a fetch is questionable. Read-only only, so the user can rerun it safely as many times as they want.

anti_patterns.dont: shell out to `benchbox-sync` as a subprocess
anti_patterns.why: the existing precedent (automate_release.py:43-49) already imports from benchbox.release; subprocess adds latency, hides errors, and complicates testing.

preserves.behavior: Default behaviour without `--allow-public-divergence` errs on the side of safety - aborting is the safe failure mode.
The `cmd_status` CLI output remains usable (no breaking change for users running `benchbox-sync status` from the shell). Internal refactor only.
The `compare_repos` function and `RepoComparison` dataclass (workflow.py:1048, :934) are unchanged - only consumed by the new function.
The existing source-side drift detection in `automate_release.py` (lines 1068, 1136-1140 - `sync_start_sha` and post-verify check) remains in place and unchanged.
The two-remote rule from CLAUDE.md - nothing in this work item should change push targets, default remotes, or the public/private rule.

work_units.notes:
1. Add to argparse (after the existing flags around automate_release.py:949):
     parser.add_argument(
         "--allow-public-divergence",
         action="store_true",
         help="Proceed even if public main has commits not present in "
              "private since the last tag (DESTRUCTIVE).",
     )
2. Insert new step between line 1063 (post-CI confirm) and line 1073
   (prepare_release call). Pseudocode:

     from benchbox.release.sync import check_public_repo_state

     print("\nStep 3.5/8: Public repo divergence preflight")
     state = check_public_repo_state(source, target)
     if state.target_exists and state.has_unexpected_divergence:
         print(f"❌ Public has commits since last tag ({state.last_tag}):")
         for line in state.commits_ahead_shas:
             print(f"     {line}")
         if state.comparison and state.comparison.has_conflicts:
             print(f"   {len(state.comparison.conflicts)} files conflict.")
         print("\n   These would be destroyed by prepare_release.py.")
         print("   Resolve:")
         print(f"     uv run -- python -m benchbox.release.sync pull "
               f"--revspec {state.last_tag}..HEAD")
         print("   ...then commit on private and re-run.")
         if not args.allow_public_divergence:
             return 1
         print("   --allow-public-divergence set, continuing (DESTRUCTIVE).")

3. Renumber subsequent step labels (Step 4/8 -> Step 4/9 etc.) so the
   progress indicators stay coherent. Or relabel as "Step 3.5/8" and
   leave existing labels - decide during implementation.
work_units.summary: Add --allow-public-divergence flag and Step 3.5 preflight to automate_release.py

work_units.notes:
At automate_release.py:1170 and :1178 (both branches of the --push if/else),
replace the line:
    print("  4. Sync fixes back to private repo:")
    print(f"     cd {source} && git push private main")
with:
    print("  4. Pull any external public changes back to private:")
    print(f"     uv run -- python -m benchbox.release.sync pull "
          f"--revspec v{version}..origin/main")
    print("     ...then commit the merged result on private.")
Rationale: a bare `git push private main` does not import public-side
community PRs. Closing the bidirectional contract is what makes the new
preflight in w4 trustworthy across releases.
work_units.summary: Update post-release print to recommend benchbox-sync pull instead of bare git push

work_units.notes:

This is the load-bearing test that the gate works.
